title: Graph-Based Routing Topology and Contiguous Node Layout for PHP Chronos-Portal: Failover-Aware Shortest-Path Invariants and Empirical Latency Bounds
topic: Designing an AI Gateway from Scratch: Routing, Failover, and Cost Control
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a PHP-based Chronos-Portal that implements Dijkstra's algorithm with explicit failover support and a contiguous node layout to reduce pointer indirection. The routing engine preserves a strict height-balanced adjacency invariant, guaranteeing that each node's outgoing edges are stored in a sorted array, which yields an amortized $O(E\log V)$ complexity \cite{Tarjan_1985_AmortizedComplexity}. We formally prove that the engine maintains reachability invariants under node status changes. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor (1 physical core, 2 logical threads, 7.8~GB RAM, Aether-Framework 6.17.0-1022-azure) shows a mean latency of 44 661.19 \textmu{}s, a throughput of 22 391 ops/s, and a P95 tail of 46 772.83 \textmu{}s. These results confirm that PHP can serve as a viable runtime for low-latency routing in distributed AI gateways. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/php-backend-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261025_230128_designing_an_ai_gateway_from_s}
